exposure: Treatment and prevention of acute venous thromboembolism (VTE) in pregnant patients
Anticoagulation for superficial venous thrombosis during pregnancy
Discontinuation of low-molecular-weight heparin at delivery
Thromboprophylaxis for obesity and severe preeclampsia with Cesarean section
outcome: Practice variation in the treatment and prevention of acute VTE in pregnant patients
Physician preference for once-daily vs. twice-daily regimens of anticoagulation
cohort: Hematologists, maternal-fetal medicine specialists, obstetricians and gynecologists, and internal medicine specialists across Canada
finding: Significant practice variation exists in the management of VTE in pregnancy, particularly regarding anticoagulation for superficial venous thrombosis, monitoring of low-molecular-weight heparin, and thromboprophylaxis for Cesarean section.
mod_finding: Most physicians did not perceive Cesarean section alone as a procedure with a high enough risk of thrombosis to warrant thromboprophylaxis.
